sections.h2: Who bills and collects the tax
sections.html:
Two city offices handle your property tax. The Assessor's Office, City Hall Room 507 at 200 E. Wells Street, sets each parcel's assessed value; call 414-286-3651. The Office of the City Treasurer, City Hall Room 103, sends the bill and takes payment; its customer services line is 414-286-2240.

Milwaukee is the Milwaukee County seat, and because the city collects its own taxes, you pay the city treasurer rather than a county office. The bill is a combined one, and special charges or assessments can be added. Any that remain unpaid in mid-November may be rolled into the property tax bill, collected as a tax, and can't be appealed, negotiated or compromised.

The city had an estimated 562,407 residents on July 1, 2025, down 2.7 percent from the April 2020 base. Only 41.8 percent of housing units are owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $184,000, median gross rent is $1,059, and the city has 232,520 households.

sections.h2: Due dates and ways to pay
sections.html:
The whole bill or the first installment is due January 31. Wis. Stat. 74.11 sets two equal installments by default, the first on or before January 31 and the second on or before July 31. A parcel with total tax under $100 is paid in full by January 31. Milwaukee also runs a longer plan, covered below.

The treasurer accepts payment these ways:

  • Mail a check using the return envelope that came with your bill. Cash isn't accepted.
  • Use a drop box. The one inside City Hall at the Market Street entrance never closes.
  • Call 414-286-2240 or go online. Cards carry a 2.75 percent convenience fee ($3.00 minimum), while ACH from a checking or savings account is free.
  • Send it through your bank's bill-pay service to City Treasurer, City Hall, Room 103, 200 East Wells Street, Milwaukee, WI 53202.

Mail early or use a drop box, because a letter in a street mailbox may not be postmarked the same day. Tyler payments made after 4:00 p.m. Central count as received the next business day.

Owners who can't pay in full can use the city's ten-month, interest-free plan. The real estate tax bill must top $100, and the first installment has to arrive by January 31. Tyler Auto Pay can draw each monthly payment from a bank account or card on its due date.

Selling partway through the ten months? Get the remaining balance from the treasurer and pass that figure to the closing agent.

The next Open Book period starts the fourth Monday in April 2027.

File a written objection with the Assessor's Office by the third Monday in May. The preferred route is the Milwaukee Real Property Appeals web application at milwaukee.gov/assessorobjection, which takes new forms only during Open Book. A paper form also works: mail it to the Assessor's Office, 200 E Wells Street, Room 507, Milwaukee, WI 53202, or hand it in Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. Forms sent by email aren't accepted and count as not filed.

Evidence can follow the form. For a house, the assessor lists:

  • An appraisal reflecting market conditions on January 1 of the current year.
  • A local agent's market analysis for that same date.
  • Photos of deferred maintenance as of January 1.
  • Photos showing a feature on your property record card wasn't there on January 1.

An appraiser reviews the appeal, and the Board of Assessors decides and mails notice. If you still disagree, ask the Board of Review clerk for a hearing at boardreview@milwaukee.gov or 414-286-3742. Under Wis. Stat. 70.47, you must tell the clerk you intend to object at least 48 hours before the board's first meeting, then file the written objection in the meeting's first two hours, unless the board waives notice for good cause. Commercial owners who skip the income and expense statement (PR-323) may be barred from testifying before the Board of Review.

Unpaid tax turns delinquent and interest starts. Wis. Stat. 74.47 sets interest on delinquent general property taxes and special charges at one percent per month or fraction of a month. A county board, or a city authorized under s. 74.87, may add a penalty of up to 0.5 percent per month by ordinance, so ask the treasurer for an exact payoff figure.

Miss the first installment by more than five working days after January 31 and the whole remaining tax is delinquent as of February 1 (s. 74.11(7)). The city's interest-free plan likewise depends on that January 31 first payment.

Most homeowners can claim the lottery and gaming credit. You must be a Wisconsin resident who owns a dwelling and lives in it as a primary residence on January 1 of the year taxes are levied. Rentals, business property, vacant land and garages don't qualify, and only one primary residence can be claimed. City properties send questions to the City of Milwaukee treasurer.

If the credit is missing from your bill, apply to the treasurer by January 31 after the bill arrives, or file a late claim with the Department of Revenue by October 1. Because the credit stays with the property, its amount should be counted when tax is prorated between buyer and seller. The assessor also publishes forms for exempt owners, with requests due March 1.

Learn what's owed before you accept an offer. The treasurer's Resident Access system shows tax bills online, and the assessor's Real Property Search shows assessed value. The assessor also posts tax rates for each year from 1984 forward, so you can see how the rate has moved.

Work through these points when you sell:

  • Get the exact balance from the treasurer, including any special charges added in November.
  • Ask your closing agent how the contract splits the bill between you and the buyer.
  • Record the deed. Any permanent change of ownership or name must be recorded with the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds.
  • Have the buyer report a mailing address change to the Assessor at City Hall Room 507, or a refund check could go to the previous owner.

With a cash buyer, taxes owed are usually paid from your proceeds at closing, so an unpaid balance doesn't have to hold up the sale. Delinquent interest keeps running until the payoff, so ask for a figure good through your closing date.

faqs.q: When are Milwaukee property taxes due?
faqs.a: The full bill or first installment is due January 31, and the state default for a second installment is July 31. The city also offers a ten-month interest-free plan for bills over $100 if the first payment arrives by January 31.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Milwaukee tax bill?
faqs.a: At the Office of the City Treasurer, City Hall, Room 103, 200 East Wells Street. You can mail a check, use a drop box, or pay by phone or online. Cash isn't accepted.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Milwaukee assessment?
faqs.a: Open Book runs from the fourth Monday in April to the third Monday in May, and that Monday is also the objection deadline each year. File with the Assessor's Office.

faqs.q: What happens if I sell a Milwaukee house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Ask the treasurer for an exact payoff first. Delinquent interest runs at one percent per month under state law, and the closing agent can pay the balance from your proceeds if your contract allows it.

faqs.q: Does Milwaukee County or the city collect my property tax?
faqs.a: The city does, through the City Treasurer. The County Register of Deeds records deeds and collects the state transfer fee.
